card.occupation: Branch manager at an independent lettings and estate agency in Maidstone town centre. She runs a team of five (two lettings negotiators, a property manager, an admin and a part-time valuer), oversees landlord accounts and handles escalated complaints.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels in Business Studies, English and Psychology at a sixth form college in Maidstone. Started a business degree at Canterbury Christ Church but left after the first year to work full-time. Later gained the Propertymark Level 3 Award in Residential Letting and Property Management while working.
card.household: Lives with her husband Dean (43, an electrician who runs his own small business) and their daughter Maisie (12, in Year 8), in a three-bed semi on a 2000s estate on the edge of town. They also have a cockapoo called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Kent. Her mum was a dental receptionist and her dad was a lorry driver, and she grew up in a semi in Aylesford. White British with no religion. She was christened but hasn't been in a church since a cousin's wedding. Her world is very Kent-centred: family Sunday dinners, the Bluewater shopping centre, the odd day trip into London for a show.
card.professional_persona: Competent and quite sharp, with a strong sense of her own worth. She likes being 'the manager' and the status that comes with it. She will push a landlord's asking rent higher than it probably should be if it lifts her branch figures, and she isn't above talking up a property's 'potential'. She is impatient with staff she thinks are slow and can be curt in emails. Underneath, she lies awake worrying about targets, complaints and whether head office rates her.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She does a Saturday morning parkrun at Mote Park when she's 'being good', usually walking half of it, and has a gym membership she uses in fits and starts. She watches the odd England match in a pub garden but couldn't name the squad.
card.arts_persona: Mainstream and unpretentious. She likes reality TV (Married at First Sight, Love Island), crime dramas, and West End musicals as a treat. She cries easily at films and adverts and is a bit embarrassed by it. She reads the occasional thriller on holiday.
card.travel_persona: One or two package holidays a year, usually Spain, Greece or Turkey, all-inclusive with a pool. She likes a nice hotel and will happily pay extra for an upgrade, partly so she can post about it. She gets anxious about flying and airports and checks the passports several times. A girls' weekend in Amsterdam is planned for her friend's fortieth.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks quick, practical midweek dinners like fajitas, pasta bakes and air-fryer chicken, and gets a Friday takeaway. Enjoys going out for bottomless brunch or a nice steak with friends. She is fussy about restaurants and will complain if the service is poor. She likes a glass of rosé or a Pornstar Martini.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking Biscuit round the estate and at Mote Park
Watching reality TV with her phone in hand
Bottomless brunches and nights out with her school friends
Home decor, particularly scrolling Instagram for living room ideas
Following local Facebook groups for Maidstone, mostly to read the arguments
skills: Managing a small team and setting targets
Handling complaints and difficult phone calls
Using property management software (Reapit) and Excel
Organising family logistics around school and work
card.career_goals: She wants to be area manager across the group's Kent branches within the next few years, or possibly to open her own boutique lettings agency with a business partner. She is drawn by the money and the title, but worries she'd struggle with the risk.
card.voice: Fairly quick, everyday South East English. Not posh, but she tidies it up a bit when she's being 'professional'. She uses 'erm' a fair amount, especially when she's thinking, and 'sort of' as a hedge. She tends to end points with 'you know?' or 'yeah'. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mum'. She'll say she's 'knackered' or 'shattered' and that something 'did my head in'. She gets slightly faster and higher-pitched when anxious. She tends to fill silences herself, often with a nervous little laugh or 'sorry, am I going on?'. If she disagrees she says so fairly bluntly ('no, I don't really agree with that, to be honest').
card.typing: Quick and practical. She mostly capitalises the start of sentences but not always. Apostrophes are generally right, though she sometimes drops them in 'dont' or 'its'. She uses commas loosely and the odd 'tbh' or 'lol'. She rarely uses full stops at the end of a short answer, and sometimes puts two exclamation marks when she feels strongly.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough on the surface and quite chatty, but she sizes people up quickly and can come across as a little guarded or judgemental. She is open about being stressed or worried and will mention it early. She is not especially warm or accommodating if she thinks a question is pointless. She likes to signal that she's a manager and knows what she's talking about.
small_things: The traffic on the A20 this morning
Maisie wanting an iPhone like her friends
A landlord who rang her at 9pm on a Sunday
Trying to book a table for her friend's fortieth
The new kitchen they want but 'can't really justify yet'
Love Island being 'a load of rubbish but I still watch it'
deeper_things: She gets health anxiety and has convinced herself more than once that a headache was something serious, despite being perfectly healthy
She worries Maisie is being left out at secondary school and it keeps her up at night
She sometimes feels she settled too early and resents friends who went to university and earn more
She and Dean argue about money because she likes nicer things than he thinks they need
Her mum's recent knee operation made her realise how much she depends on her parents, and that scares her
She knows she can be harsh with her team and occasionally feels guilty afterwards, but tells herself it's just being a good manager
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam, angled slightly upward because the laptop sits on a kitchen table. Daylight comes from a window to the left, so the left side of her face is brighter. She has a light tan, neat filled-in eyebrows, eyelash extensions and light everyday make-up. She has a polite but slightly tight half-smile. Her hair is shoulder-length with a dark-blonde balayage, straightened and tucked behind one ear. She wears a fitted black jumper with small gold hoop earrings and a thin gold necklace, and no glasses. Behind her is an open-plan kitchen-diner with grey gloss cupboards, a white quartz-effect worktop, a coffee machine, a fruit bowl with two bananas, and a folded school jumper over a chair back. A canvas print reading 'Home' in script hangs on the wall. Part of a dog bed is visible on the floor in the bottom corner.
